newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen rising at open on Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen rising at open on Greenspan.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to open higher on Friday, helped by bullishly interpreted remarks from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
At a dinner on Thursday, Greenspan made remarks which were seen by the market as a hint that an interest rate hike may not be in the offing on May 20.
But he did say that the Fed would act appropriately if the U.S. economy did not slow as expected. U.S. bonds rose on the back of Greenspan's words.
On Thursday, the Toronto Stock Exchange key 300 Composite Index rose 35.92 points to close at 6157.44.
"(Stocks are) going higher because Greenspan sort of mumbled that they may not have to make a move on rates this month," said one trader.
He said New York looked likely to increase about 35 points at the open.
"We'll probably tag along for the ride," he added.
Interest-rate sensitive shares such as high-yield conglomerates, utilities and bank shares should profit most from the easing rate fears.
Canada's unemployment rate jumped to 9.6 percent in April, Statistics Canada said on Friday in its last such release before the June 2 federal election.
The main reason for the rise was because 79,000 people joined the work force, swamping the estimated 33,000 jobs that were added, mostly in self-employment. Total employment was 13.83 million.
Economists said the focus should be on the employment growth rather than on the unemployment rate.
